_comment: How Tools/Blender/build_ai_ship.py turns the Meshy 'Ironclad Starfighter' export into Vanguard_Meshy.blend. Coordinates are Blender metres after orienting and scaling: +X nose, +Y the ship's left, +Z up. Measured on the oriented model (18. 9. 2026): 14.0 x 11.44 x 6.18 m, one connected surface; four engine nacelles (centres y +-4.3, z +1.8 / -1.1), nozzles recessed at x -5.8 .. -6.7; skids fused into the hull: one nose skid on the centreline (x 1.7 .. 3.6, 1.1 m under the belly at -2.0) and two main skids at y +-2.0 .. 2.75 (x -4.6 .. -2.6, 0.55 m under the belly at -2.56); cabin x 2 .. 4.5, roof 1.6 .. 2.1 m.

Gear._comment: Everything wholly below the belly at the skids. The stubs between belly and cut stay on the hull as mounts.

decimate._comment: Importance 1 = keep detail, 0 = decimate freely; the last matching rule wins. protect_factor scales how much importance matters. 20. 9. 2026: the hull keeps 1 million triangles instead of 200 thousand (the author found it too soft up close in the chase camera). Nanite draws it at whatever detail the screen needs, so the cost is the file and the bake time, not the frame; the original Meshy model has 3.36 million.

importance._what: upward faces (seen from the chase camera)
inside the nozzles and the rear bulkhead

rebake._comment: New UV atlas on the decimated meshes and the full-resolution model baked onto it (Cycles, selected to active). Meshy's own atlas has thousands of tiny islands that decimation welds together, and its normal map is almost flat: the detail is geometry.

emissive._comment: Nozzle discs get the M_Ship_<Ship>_Emissive slot, which the game makes glow with engine load.

canopy_clear._comment: From the seat the frame between the windscreen and the roof panes (its underside, invisible from outside behind the opaque panes) crossed the HUD 4 degrees above the eye line. Faces in the canopy that point towards the cabin's axis (y 0, z axis_z) are deleted.

canopy_frame._comment: Inside of the canopy frame, as the pilot sees it: its own dark slot (MI_Ship_Vanguard_CanopyFrame). With the hull's paint the frame struts caught the sun and read as bright wires across the view.

lining._comment: From the cockpit the one-sided hull was invisible: the pilot looked through the floor and the sides at the ground. The fuselage around and behind the cabin is copied with inward normals; the canopy glass (above the rail, x 1.9 .. 4.8) is left out so the view stays open.

collision.name: canopy (own hull: remove it for a modelled cockpit interior)

Cockpit._comment: The pilot's eye, 65 cm behind the side grips of the cockpit interior with a clear view ahead, the dashboard top ~8 degrees below (Tools/Blender/fit_ship_interior.py; framing checked against the SC reference with Tools/Shots.ps1 -Preset cockpit_tune). 19. 9. 2026: moved 20 cm nearer the dashboard and 3 cm lower (the author found the displays' figures too small from the fitted eye), with the view tilted 3 degrees down in the setup (cockpit_view_pitch_deg).

Exit._comment: beside the cabin on the right (Blender -Y), on the ground

interior._comment: Meshy 'Spaceship Cockpit', dark variant (18. 9. 2026, replaced the grey 0918112024 one): a U-shaped dashboard with two big displays, two small squares between them, a centre column with a stick, side consoles and two side grips, 1.27 M triangles, no floor, no seat, no canopy; matt (metallic 0, roughness ~0.62), dark grey paint. Forward along +Y, hence -90 degrees. Placement from Tools/Blender/fit_ship_interior.py: inside the hull everywhere (2 cm), rim ~10 cm from the cabin walls, eye 65 cm behind the side grips with a clear view ahead, dashboard top 8 degrees and the displays 14-25 degrees below the eye (reference: 8 and 15-24) - the pilot sits well back from the dashboard, as in the Star Citizen reference (Docs/UI/Screenshot 2026-09-17 201854.png), not close over it as with the first interior.

fit._comment: Search limits for fit_ship_interior.py; stick_grip = top of the side grips in the rotated, unscaled model. dash_below_eye_deg 7-13 and 65 cm behind the grips: the reference's dashboard sits ~8 degrees under the eye with the pilot ~1.2 m from it; 14-22 degrees and 15 cm put the first interior almost in the pilot's lap.

rebake._comment: 4K: the dashboard is 0.8 m from the eye; with 2K and an even atlas the displays were blurred. Shorter bake rays (1 cm cage, 4 cm reach): longer ones caught neighbouring surfaces and left white flecks on the frames.

uv_focus._comment: More texture for what the pilot sees: UV islands facing the eye (sockets.Cockpit) within 2 m get 3x the area before packing.

displays._comment: The two big displays, in the rotated, unscaled model: centre, u = the screen's right, v = its up, and the corners of the bezel opening (top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left, metres in u / v). The openings are not rectangles (slanted sides, the right one leans); the corners were fitted by eye in the live Blender viewport from the pilot's eye with a measuring grid on the display plane (Blender MCP, 19. 9. 2026). The AI glass inside the outline is cut, a flat quad takes its place; the game draws its displays into the texture of slot M_Ship_Vanguard_Screens: left display = left half, right display = right half (UCockpitDisplayComponent). The centre column's two small screens (centre_top: radar, centre_bottom: self status) were measured the same way (19. 9. 2026): ray casts from the eye fitted their glass plane (the same tilt as the big displays), a flood fill found the openings, and outlines drawn in the live viewport were corrected by eye - the bottom edges are level, a knob on the bezel sits at each bottom-right corner (cut_depth_m 6 mm: only the glass is cut, the knobs stay). texture_size / texture_rect: where each screen is on the game's canvas (USpaceCockpitDisplays::ScreenRect), the same pixels per centimetre on every screen. grow_m 0.0045 (~5 mm in the game): the screens reach that far under the bezel lips beyond the cut outline - fitted exactly, the AI glass still showed as thin light strips at some corners (author's close-ups, 19. 9. 2026); 0 / 5 / 8 mm compared in the live viewport from the eye, 5 mm fills every opening, 8 mm adds nothing.
